newsitem.title: UK: DOLLAR, WEATHER TO RULE IN EURO VEG OILS.
newsitem.headline: DOLLAR, WEATHER TO RULE IN EURO VEG OILS.

text.p: Trading on the European vegetable oil market is set to remain under the twin influences of the dollar and the U.S. Midwest weather in the week ahead.
The strong dollar against the Malaysian ringgit and its effect on palm oil exports will rule that sector.
Traders said a weak ringgit should boost exports of palm oil which has become cheaper in dollar terms against soft oils.
So far export figures seem to be bearing this out, but rising Malaysian output could limit the upside of the market.

Traders said Indonesia has been very competitive and exports to Europe are high, but this is causing some tightness in the local market and combined with the higher prices could triggered intervention from the state logistics agency BULOG.
"The dollar is playing havoc with the market and people really don't know what to do for the best," said one trader.
The lauric oils sector is expected to take its cue from palm oil with sellers tracking the firmer prices, but buyers are not likely to follow very closely owing to rising production at origin.
In the soft oil sector the dollar and weather will combine to control prices.
If the dollar remains firm this will limit the down of the market should Chicago futures fall.
But higher Chicago futures and a firm dollar will only frighten buyers off.
Rape oil will to some extent be affected by the dollar and Chicago but nearby months will see increasing pressure from the harvest.
